'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[2025 Shabelle offensive]]
***[[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] militants reportedly seize control of Hawadley village in the [[Middle Shabelle]] region of [[Hirshabelle State]] following the withdrawal of [[Burundi National Defence Force|Burundian forces]] under the [[African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia|AUSSOM]] from the strategic military base. [https://en.kaabtv.com/al-shabaab-militants-seize-control-of-hawadley-in-middle-shabelle-region/ (Kaab TV)] [https://www.ftlsomalia.com/al-shabaab-seizes-hawadley-after-au-forces-withdraw/amp/ (FTL Somalia)]
*[[War against the Islamic State]]
**[[American military intervention in Somalia (2007–present)|American military intervention in Somalia]]
***[[New America (organization)|New America]], a [[Washington, D.C.]]-based [[think tank]], reports that [[Drone strikes in Somalia|U.S. airstrikes]] in [[Somalia]] targeting Al-Shabaab and [[Islamic State]] militants resulted in up to 174 fatalities, including an estimated six to 30 civilian casualties, in 2025. [https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/us-airstrikes-in-somalia-killed-up-to-174-people-in-2025-monitoring-group-says (Garowe Online)] [https://www.newamerica.org/future-security/reports/americas-counterterrorism-wars/the-war-in-somalia/ (New America)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Five police officers are killed after an ambush in a highway in the border municipality of [[Frontera Comalapa]]. Hours later, an attacker was arrested and authorities confirmed that the attack was a retaliation for the recent arrest of Aler Baldomero Samayoa Recinos, also known as “Chicharra,” leader of Los Huistas, a Guatemalan criminal group that established ties with both the [[Sinaloa Cartel]] and the [[CJNG]]. [https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/estados/2025/6/3/detienen-uno-de-los-presuntos-responsables-de-emboscar-calcinar-cinco-policias-en-chiapas-352353.html (Revista Proceso)]
*[[Cambodia]] says it will seek a ruling from the [[United Nations]]'s [[International Court of Justice]] over border disputes with [[Thailand]], which triggered a fatal military clash last week. [https://apnews.com/article/cambodia-thailand-border-court-preah-vihear-dispute-ed4967fb809448ccf42542ea21de9839 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[North Macedonia–United States relations]]
**[[North Macedonia]] announces that it will remove [[import tax]]es on U.S. goods to seek a reciprocal measure from the [[United States]], as [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (North Macedonia)|Foreign Minister]] [[Timčo Mucunski]] says that the country is negotiating a free trade agreement with the U.S. [https://apnews.com/article/north-macedonia-united-states-tariffs-trump-6ef2fed0413db8d6967ad4bb4153f05f (AP)]
*[[Government procurement in the European Union|Procurement in the European Union]]
**The [[European Commission]] passes a measure to limit [[China|Chinese]] [[medical device]] supply bids on public contracts, alleging unfair access for [[EU]] companies to China's tenders. The measures are the first under the International Procurement Instrument. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/eu-backs-curbs-chinese-medical-device-firms-bidding-public-tenders-2025-06-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
**[[United States]] [[Midwestern United States|Midwest]] [[aluminum]] premiums rise by 164% after demand for aluminum in the physical market increased due to US president [[Donald Trump]]'s plan to increase [[tariff]]s on imported [[steel]] and aluminum from 25% to 50%. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aluminium-premium-us-buyers-soars-after-trump-doubles-tariffs-2025-06-02/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Damascus Securities Exchange]] reopens in [[Syria]] after six months of closure following the [[fall of the Assad regime]] in December 2024. [https://english.alarabiya.net/business/economy/2025/06/02/damascus-stock-exchange-reopens-after-6month-closure (Al Arabiya)]
*The [[Philippine]] [[Department of Transportation (Philippines)|Department of Transportation]] orders [[AirAsia]] to halt the sale of airline tickets in the country, citing alleged overpricing after reports revealed that fares on the airline's website significantly exceeded government-approved [[price ceiling]]s. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-06-02/philippines-orders-airasia-move-shutdown-on-excessive-pricing (Bloomberg)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Nigeria floods]]
**[[2025 Mokwa flood]]
***The death toll from the [[flooding]] caused by torrential rain in [[Mokwa]], [[Nigeria]], increases to over 200. [https://www.dw.com/en/death-toll-in-nigeria-flooding-rises-to-at-least-200/video-72755995 (DW)]
*A 41-year-old ski mountaineer dies after falling 3,000 feet while climbing [[Mount McKinley]]. His body was discovered two days later, on June 4. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/climber-falls-3000-feet-death-off-tallest-mountain/story?id=122522462 (ABC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**[[U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces that the recent [[U.S.]] proposal for a deal on [[Iran]]'s [[nuclear program of Iran|nuclear program]] does not allow any [[enriched uranium|uranium enrichment]] by Iran, despite previous media reports to the contrary. [https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20250602-trump-iran-uranium-enrichment-nuclear (France24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russia]] and [[Ukraine]] hold further negotiations in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]], resulting in an agreement for a [[prisoner of war]] [[Prisoner exchange|exchange]]. Officials confirm that all sick and severely wounded prisoners of war, along with those younger than 25, will be exchanged. Russia and Ukraine also exchanged [[ceasefire]] proposals during the negotiations. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cgrg7kelk45t (BBC News)]
*A [[Sweden|Swedish]] commission recommends that [[international adoption]]s be stopped after an investigation found a series of [[abuse]]s and [[fraud]] dating back decades. The commission was formed in 2021 following a report by Swedish newspaper ''[[Dagens Nyheter]]'' detailing Sweden's problematic international adoption system. [https://apnews.com/article/sweden-adoption-846ce8d1fd20b680247254bc86eb4fee (AP)]
